source.text: Καὶ ὅταν ἤνοιξεν τὴν σφραγῖδα τὴν ἑβδόμην, ἐγένετο σιγὴ ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ ὡς ἡμιώριον.

records.literal_gloss: And when he opened the seal the seventh, there was silence in the heaven about half an hour.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke the seventh seal, heaven fell silent for about half an hour.
en.R: When the Lamb opened the seventh seal, everything in heaven was silent for about half an hour.

fr.L: Et quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ouvrit le septième sceau, il se fit un silence dans le ciel d’environ une demi-heure.
fr.B: Quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} brisa le septième sceau, le ciel fit silence pendant environ une demi-heure.
fr.R: Quand l’Agneau a ouvert le septième sceau, tout est devenu silencieux dans le ciel pendant environ une demi-heure.

es.L: Y cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} abrió el séptimo sello, hubo silencio en el cielo como por media hora.
es.B: Cuando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} rompió el séptimo sello, el cielo quedó en silencio durante una media hora.
es.R: Cuando el Cordero abrió el séptimo sello, todo quedó en silencio en el cielo durante una media hora.

decisions.choice: silence in heaven: awe before God acts
alternatives: a silence so that the prayers of the saints can be heard (8:3-4)
decisions.reason: The praise of chapters 4-7 stops. The prophets call for silence before the Lord as he comes to judge: "Be silent before the Lord GOD, for the day of the LORD is near" (Zephaniah 1:7; compare Habakkuk 2:20; Zechariah 2:13). The silence may also make room for the prayers that rise in 8:3-4.

decisions.choice: when: a single event
decisions.reason: ὅταν usually means "whenever", but here it is used with a past verb for one event, as "when".

decisions.choice: the seventh seal opens into the seven trumpets
decisions.reason: The seventh seal brings no horse or disaster of its own. Out of its silence come the seven angels with trumpets (8:2), so that the trumpets unfold what the last seal holds.

decisions.choice: John's visions told in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("il ouvrit", "je vis") and the passé composé at Readable ("a ouvert", "j’ai vu")
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for Revelation, and as in chapters 6 and 7. This holds for the whole chapter.

source.text: καὶ εἶδον τοὺς ἑπτὰ ἀγγέλους οἳ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ἑστήκασιν, καὶ ἐδόθησαν αὐτοῖς ἑπτὰ σάλπιγγες.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw the seven angels who before the God stand, and were given to them seven trumpets.

en.L: And I saw the seven angels who stand before God, and seven trumpets were given to them.
en.B: And I saw the seven angels who stand in God's presence; they were given seven trumpets.
en.R: Then I saw the seven angels who stand in front of God. They were given seven trumpets.

fr.L: Et je vis les sept anges qui se tiennent devant Dieu, et sept trompettes leur furent données.
fr.B: Et je vis les sept anges qui se tiennent en présence de Dieu ; on leur donna sept trompettes.
fr.R: Ensuite, j’ai vu les sept anges qui se tiennent devant Dieu. On leur a donné sept trompettes.

es.L: Y vi a los siete ángeles que están de pie delante de Dios, y se les dieron siete trompetas.
es.B: Y vi a los siete ángeles que están en la presencia de Dios; se les dieron siete trompetas.
es.R: Luego vi a los siete ángeles que están de pie delante de Dios. Les dieron siete trompetas.

decisions.choice: the seven angels who stand before God
decisions.reason: The article, "the seven angels", suggests a known group. Jewish writings of the time speak of seven angels who stand in God's presence: in Tobit 12:15 Raphael calls himself "one of the seven angels who stand ready and enter before the glory of the Lord", and 1 Enoch 20 names seven archangels.

decisions.choice: trumpets: signals of war, alarm and the day of the Lord
decisions.reason: Trumpets called Israel to battle and to festivals, and they sounded at the fall of Jericho (Joshua 6). The prophets announce the day of the Lord with a trumpet blast (Joel 2:1; Zephaniah 1:14-16).

source.text: Καὶ ἄλλος ἄγγελος ἦλθεν καὶ ἐστάθη ἐπὶ τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου ἔχων λιβανωτὸν χρυσοῦν, καὶ ἐδόθη αὐτῷ θυμιάματα πολλὰ ἵνα δώσει ταῖς προσευχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων πάντων ἐπὶ τὸ θυσιαστήριον τὸ χρυσοῦν τὸ ἐνώπιον τοῦ θρόνου.

records.literal_gloss: And another angel came and stood at the altar having a censer golden, and was given to him incenses many so that he will give with the prayers of the saints all on the altar the golden the [one] before the throne.

en.L: And another angel came and stood at the altar, having a golden censer, and much incense was given to him, so that he might offer [it] with the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar that [is] before the throne.
en.B: Then another angel came, holding a gold censer, and took his place at the altar. Much incense was handed to him, so that he could add it to the prayers of all God's holy people on the gold altar before the throne.
en.R: Another angel came and stood at the altar. He had a gold pan for burning incense. He was given a lot of incense to offer to God along with the prayers of all God's people. He offered it on the gold altar in front of the throne.

fr.L: Et un autre ange vint et se tint près de l’autel, ayant un encensoir d’or, et beaucoup d’encens lui fut donné, afin qu’il [l’]offre avec les prières de tous les saints sur l’autel d’or qui [est] devant le trône.
fr.B: Puis un autre ange vint, tenant un encensoir d’or, et se plaça près de l’autel. On lui remit beaucoup d’encens, pour qu’il l’ajoute aux prières de tout le peuple saint de Dieu sur l’autel d’or qui est devant le trône.
fr.R: Un autre ange est venu se placer près de l’autel. Il avait un récipient en or pour brûler l’encens. On lui a donné beaucoup d’encens, pour qu’il l’offre à Dieu avec les prières de tout le peuple de Dieu. Il l’a offert sur l’autel en or, devant le trône.

es.L: Y otro ángel vino y se puso de pie junto al altar, con un incensario de oro, y se le dio mucho incienso para que [lo] ofreciera con las oraciones de todos los santos sobre el altar de oro que [está] delante del trono.
es.B: Entonces vino otro ángel con un incensario de oro y se colocó junto al altar. Se le entregó mucho incienso para que lo añadiera a las oraciones de todo el pueblo santo de Dios sobre el altar de oro que está delante del trono.
es.R: Vino otro ángel y se puso de pie junto al altar. Tenía un recipiente de oro para quemar incienso. Le dieron mucho incienso para que lo ofreciera a Dios junto con las oraciones de todo el pueblo de Dios. Lo ofreció sobre el altar de oro que está delante del trono.

decisions.choice: a censer and the golden altar: the altar of incense
decisions.reason: λιβανωτὸν was a vessel for carrying burning coals and incense. The golden altar stood before the inner room of the tabernacle and temple, and incense was burned on it morning and evening (Exodus 30:1-10). In heaven it stands before God's throne.

decisions.choice: the incense is added to the prayers
alternatives: the incense is the prayers, as in 5:8
decisions.reason: "Offer with the prayers" most likely means that the incense goes up together with the prayers and carries them to God. In 5:8 the incense is the prayers; the picture is close.

decisions.choice: the prayers of all the saints, including the martyrs' cry of 6:10
decisions.reason: The prayers of God's people (5:8) include the cry of the martyrs under the altar for justice (6:9-10). What follows in 8:5 is God's answer.

decisions.choice: censer (L, B); pan for burning incense (R)
decisions.reason: Readable describes the vessel, since few young readers know the word "censer".

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

decisions.choice: les saints (L); le peuple saint de Dieu (B); le peuple de Dieu (R) (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term for God's holy people, as the English has it. French "les saints" usually means canonised saints, so Balanced and Readable say who they are.

decisions.choice: incensario (L, B); un recipiente de oro para quemar incienso (R)
decisions.reason: "Incensario" is the ordinary Spanish word for the vessel in which incense is burned, and it is used again in 8:5. Readable says what it is in plain words, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἀνέβη ὁ καπνὸς τῶν θυμιαμάτων ταῖς προσευχαῖς τῶν ἁγίων ἐκ χειρὸς τοῦ ἀγγέλου ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And went up the smoke of the incenses with the prayers of the saints out of hand of the angel before the God.

en.L: And the smoke of the incense went up with the prayers of the saints from the hand of the angel before God.
en.B: The smoke of the incense rose with the prayers of God's holy people from the angel's hand before God.
en.R: The smoke from the incense went up to God from the angel's hand, together with the prayers of God's people.

fr.L: Et la fumée de l’encens monta avec les prières des saints, de la main de l’ange, devant Dieu.
fr.B: La fumée de l’encens s’éleva, avec les prières du peuple saint de Dieu, de la main de l’ange devant Dieu.
fr.R: La fumée de l’encens est montée vers Dieu depuis la main de l’ange, avec les prières du peuple de Dieu.

es.L: Y el humo del incienso subió con las oraciones de los santos, de la mano del ángel, delante de Dios.
es.B: El humo del incienso subió, con las oraciones del pueblo santo de Dios, desde la mano del ángel hasta la presencia de Dios.
es.R: El humo del incienso subió hasta Dios desde la mano del ángel, junto con las oraciones del pueblo de Dios.

decisions.choice: prayer rising like incense: Psalm 141:2
decisions.reason: "Let my prayer be counted as incense before you" (Psalm 141:2). The prayers of God's people reach him.

decisions.choice: saints (L); God's holy people (B); God's people (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:8.

source.text: καὶ εἴληφεν ὁ ἄγγελος τὸν λιβανωτόν, καὶ ἐγέμισεν αὐτὸν ἐκ τοῦ πυρὸς τοῦ θυσιαστηρίου, καὶ ἔβαλεν εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ ἐγένοντο βρονταὶ καὶ φωναὶ καὶ ἀστραπαὶ καὶ σεισμός.

records.literal_gloss: And has taken the angel the censer and filled it out of the fire of the altar and threw to the earth, and there were thunders and voices and lightnings and earthquake.

en.L: And the angel took the censer and filled it with the fire of the altar and threw [it] to the earth, and there were thunders and voices and lightnings and an earthquake.
en.B: The angel then took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and flung it onto the earth. Thunder crashed, there were loud sounds and lightning, and the earth shook.
en.R: Then the angel took the incense pan and filled it with fire from the altar. He threw it down on the earth. There was thunder, loud noise, lightning, and an earthquake.

fr.L: Et l’ange prit l’encensoir, et le remplit du feu de l’autel, et [le] jeta sur la terre ; et il y eut des tonnerres, et des voix, et des éclairs, et un tremblement de terre.
fr.B: L’ange prit alors l’encensoir, le remplit du feu de l’autel et le lança sur la terre. Il y eut des coups de tonnerre, des fracas et des éclairs, et la terre trembla.
fr.R: Ensuite, l’ange a pris le récipient à encens et l’a rempli de feu pris sur l’autel. Il l’a jeté sur la terre. Il y a eu du tonnerre, des bruits forts, des éclairs et un tremblement de terre.

es.L: Y el ángel tomó el incensario, y lo llenó del fuego del altar, y [lo] arrojó a la tierra; y hubo truenos y voces y relámpagos y un terremoto.
es.B: Luego el ángel tomó el incensario, lo llenó con fuego del altar y lo lanzó sobre la tierra. Retumbaron truenos, hubo estruendos y relámpagos, y la tierra tembló.
es.R: Después el ángel tomó el recipiente del incienso y lo llenó con fuego del altar. Lo arrojó sobre la tierra. Hubo truenos, ruidos fuertes, relámpagos y un terremoto.

decisions.choice: fire thrown on the earth: Ezekiel 10
decisions.reason: In Ezekiel 10:2 a man clothed in linen fills his hands with burning coals from between the cherubim and scatters them over Jerusalem in judgment. The same altar from which the prayers rose sends down fire: the prayers of the saints are answered in judgment.

decisions.choice: thunder, voices, lightning and earthquake
decisions.reason: The signs of God's presence at Sinai and around the throne (4:5) now come to the earth, with an earthquake added. The list grows at each stage (11:19; 16:18-21).

decisions.choice: voices (L); loud sounds (B); loud noise (R)
decisions.reason: As in 4:5, the word means loud sounds or rumblings.

source.text: Καὶ οἱ ἑπτὰ ἄγγελοι οἱ ἔχοντες τὰς ἑπτὰ σάλπιγγας ἡτοίμασαν αὑτοὺς ἵνα σαλπίσωσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And the seven angels the [ones] having the seven trumpets prepared themselves so that they might blow trumpets.

en.L: And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to blow [them].
en.B: Then the seven angels holding the seven trumpets made ready to blow them.
en.R: Then the seven angels who had the seven trumpets got ready to blow them.

fr.L: Et les sept anges qui avaient les sept trompettes se préparèrent pour sonner [de la trompette].
fr.B: Alors les sept anges qui tenaient les sept trompettes se préparèrent à en sonner.
fr.R: Ensuite, les sept anges qui avaient les sept trompettes se sont préparés à sonner de la trompette.

es.L: Y los siete ángeles que tenían las siete trompetas se prepararon para tocar[las].
es.B: Entonces los siete ángeles que tenían las siete trompetas se dispusieron a tocarlas.
es.R: Luego los siete ángeles que tenían las siete trompetas se prepararon para tocarlas.

decisions.choice: the trumpets now begin
decisions.reason: After the interruption of 8:3-5, John returns to the seven angels of 8:2. The first four trumpets (8:7-12) strike the natural world; the last three are announced as "woes" (8:13).

source.text: Καὶ ὁ πρῶτος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἐγένετο χάλαζα καὶ πῦρ μεμιγμένα ἐν αἵματι, καὶ ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν γῆν· καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῆς γῆς κατεκάη, καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν δένδρων κατεκάη, καὶ πᾶς χόρτος χλωρὸς κατεκάη.

records.literal_gloss: And the first blew trumpet, and there was hail and fire having been mixed in blood, and it was thrown to the earth; and the third of the earth was burned up, and the third of the trees was burned up, and all grass green was burned up.

en.L: And the first blew his trumpet, and there was hail and fire mixed with blood, and it was thrown to the earth, and a third of the earth was burned up, and a third of the trees was burned up, and all green grass was burned up.
en.B: When the first angel blew his trumpet, hail and fire, mixed with blood, were flung down on the earth. A third of the land was burned up, and a third of the trees, and every green blade of grass.
en.R: The first angel blew his trumpet. Hail and fire mixed with blood were thrown down on the earth. A third of the earth burned up. A third of the trees burned up. All the green grass burned up.

fr.L: Et le premier sonna de la trompette ; et il y eut de la grêle et du feu mêlés de sang, et cela fut jeté sur la terre ; et le tiers de la terre fut brûlé, et le tiers des arbres fut brûlé, et toute herbe verte fut brûlée.
fr.B: Quand le premier ange sonna de la trompette, de la grêle et du feu mêlés de sang furent lancés sur la terre. Le tiers de la terre fut consumé, ainsi que le tiers des arbres et toute l’herbe verte.
fr.R: Le premier ange a sonné de la trompette. De la grêle et du feu mêlés de sang ont été jetés sur la terre. Un tiers de la terre a brûlé. Un tiers des arbres a brûlé. Toute l’herbe verte a brûlé.

es.L: Y el primero tocó la trompeta, y hubo granizo y fuego mezclados con sangre, y fueron arrojados a la tierra; y la tercera parte de la tierra se quemó, y la tercera parte de los árboles se quemó, y toda la hierba verde se quemó.
es.B: Cuando el primer ángel tocó su trompeta, granizo y fuego mezclados con sangre fueron lanzados sobre la tierra. Se quemó la tercera parte de la tierra, la tercera parte de los árboles y toda la hierba verde.
es.R: El primer ángel tocó su trompeta. Granizo y fuego mezclados con sangre fueron arrojados sobre la tierra. Se quemó la tercera parte de la tierra. Se quemó la tercera parte de los árboles. Se quemó toda la hierba verde.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: hail and fire
decisions.reason: The trumpets recall the plagues God sent on Egypt before the exodus (Exodus 9:23-25). As then, God judges a power that oppresses his people, and those he has sealed are spared (7:3; 9:4).

decisions.choice: a third: judgment that is severe but partial
decisions.reason: The seals struck a quarter of the earth (6:8); the trumpets strike a third. The harm is great but not complete. These judgments are warnings that call people to repent, as 9:20-21 shows, before the final judgment.

decisions.choice: all green grass
decisions.reason: Here all the green grass burns, yet in 9:4 the locusts are told not to harm the grass. The visions are pictures of judgment and do not form a single sequence of events in which each detail must agree with the last.

decisions.choice: blew his trumpet
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to blow a trumpet. Every level says so plainly; "his trumpet" is supplied.

decisions.choice: sonner de la trompette, without "sa" (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: French says the Greek verb in one fixed phrase, "sonner de la trompette", which needs no possessive, so the "his" the English supplies is not needed. "Souffler dans sa trompette" sounds childish.

decisions.choice: tocó la trompeta (L); tocó su trompeta (B, R) (for the whole book)
decisions.reason: The Greek has a single verb, "trumpeted". Spanish says it with "tocar la trompeta", the ordinary way to say an instrument is played; Literal keeps the bare article, Balanced and Readable say "su trompeta" as the English says "his trumpet". The same wording is used for each of the seven angels.

decisions.choice: la tercera parte
decisions.reason: "La tercera parte" is the natural Spanish way to speak of a third of a whole, and it is kept at every level and for every trumpet so the repeated measure of the judgment stays visible.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ δεύτερος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ὡς ὄρος μέγα πυρὶ καιόμενον ἐβλήθη εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν· καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ τρίτον τῆς θαλάσσης αἷμα, καὶ ἀπέθανε τὸ τρίτον τῶν κτισμάτων τῶν ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, τὰ ἔχοντα ψυχάς, καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν πλοίων διεφθάρησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And the second angel blew trumpet, and as a mountain great with fire burning was thrown into the sea; and became the third of the sea blood, \v 9 and died the third of the creatures the [ones] in the sea, those having lives, and the third of the ships were destroyed.

en.L: And the second angel blew his trumpet, and [something] like a great mountain burning with fire was thrown into the sea, and a third of the sea became blood, \v 9 and a third of the creatures in the sea, those that had life, died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
en.B: Then the second angel blew his trumpet. What looked like a great mountain on fire was hurled into the sea, and a third of the sea became blood. \v 9 Of the creatures living in the sea a third died, and of the ships a third were wrecked.
en.R: The second angel blew his trumpet. Something like a huge mountain on fire was thrown into the sea. A third of the sea turned into blood. \v 9 A third of the living things in the sea died. A third of the ships were destroyed.

fr.L: Et le deuxième ange sonna de la trompette ; et comme une grande montagne brûlant de feu fut jetée dans la mer ; et le tiers de la mer devint du sang, \v 9 et le tiers des créatures qui [sont] dans la mer, celles qui avaient vie, mourut, et le tiers des navires fut détruit.
fr.B: Puis le deuxième ange sonna de la trompette. Ce qui ressemblait à une grande montagne en feu fut précipité dans la mer, et le tiers de la mer devint du sang. \v 9 Des créatures qui vivaient dans la mer, le tiers mourut, et des navires, le tiers fit naufrage.
fr.R: Le deuxième ange a sonné de la trompette. Quelque chose comme une énorme montagne en feu a été jeté dans la mer. Un tiers de la mer s’est changé en sang. \v 9 Un tiers des êtres vivants de la mer sont morts. Un tiers des bateaux ont été détruits.

es.L: Y el segundo ángel tocó la trompeta, y [algo] como una gran montaña ardiendo con fuego fue arrojado al mar; y la tercera parte del mar se convirtió en sangre, \v 9 y murió la tercera parte de las criaturas que [estaban] en el mar, las que tenían vida, y la tercera parte de las naves fue destruida.
es.B: Luego el segundo ángel tocó su trompeta. Algo que parecía una gran montaña en llamas fue lanzado al mar, y la tercera parte del mar se convirtió en sangre. \v 9 Murió la tercera parte de los seres que viven en el mar, y la tercera parte de los barcos quedó destruida.
es.R: El segundo ángel tocó su trompeta. Algo parecido a una enorme montaña en llamas fue arrojado al mar. La tercera parte del mar se convirtió en sangre. \v 9 Murió la tercera parte de los seres vivos del mar. Fue destruida la tercera parte de los barcos.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: water turned to blood
decisions.reason: The trumpets recall the plagues God sent on Egypt before the exodus (Exodus 7:20-21). As then, God judges a power that oppresses his people, and those he has sealed are spared (7:3; 9:4).

decisions.choice: a burning mountain: Jeremiah's word against Babylon
decisions.reason: God calls Babylon a "destroying mountain" and says he will make it "a burnt mountain" (Jeremiah 51:25). The picture may hint at the fall of a great power. John says only that it was "like" a mountain.

decisions.choice: a third: judgment that is severe but partial
decisions.reason: The seals struck a quarter of the earth (6:8); the trumpets strike a third. The harm is great but not complete. These judgments are warnings that call people to repent, as 9:20-21 shows, before the final judgment.

decisions.choice: blew his trumpet
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to blow a trumpet. Every level says so plainly; "his trumpet" is supplied.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ τρίτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ ἀστὴρ μέγας καιόμενος ὡς λαμπάς, καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν ποταμῶν καὶ ἐπὶ τὰς πηγὰς τῶν ὑδάτων.

records.literal_gloss: And the third angel blew trumpet, and fell out of the heaven a star great burning like a torch, and it fell on the third of the rivers and on the springs of the waters.

en.L: And the third angel blew his trumpet, and a great star fell from heaven, burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of waters.
en.B: The third angel blew his trumpet, and down from the sky came a huge star, burning like a torch. It landed on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.
en.R: The third angel blew his trumpet. A huge star fell from the sky. It was burning like a torch. It fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of water.

fr.L: Et le troisième ange sonna de la trompette ; et il tomba du ciel une grande étoile, brûlant comme une torche, et elle tomba sur le tiers des fleuves et sur les sources des eaux.
fr.B: Le troisième ange sonna de la trompette, et du ciel tomba une étoile immense, qui brûlait comme une torche. Elle tomba sur le tiers des fleuves et sur les sources d’eau.
fr.R: Le troisième ange a sonné de la trompette. Une énorme étoile est tombée du ciel. Elle brûlait comme une torche. Elle est tombée sur un tiers des rivières et sur les sources d’eau.

es.L: Y el tercer ángel tocó la trompeta, y cayó del cielo una gran estrella, ardiendo como una antorcha, y cayó sobre la tercera parte de los ríos y sobre los manantiales de las aguas.
es.B: El tercer ángel tocó su trompeta, y del cielo cayó una enorme estrella que ardía como una antorcha. Cayó sobre la tercera parte de los ríos y sobre los manantiales de agua.
es.R: El tercer ángel tocó su trompeta. Una enorme estrella cayó del cielo. Ardía como una antorcha. Cayó sobre la tercera parte de los ríos y sobre los manantiales de agua.

decisions.choice: a star falling from heaven
alternatives: an angel, as the star in 9:1 is
decisions.reason: Isaiah 14:12 speaks of the king of Babylon as a star fallen from heaven. In 9:1 a fallen star is a being who is given a key. Here the star is the means of the plague, and its name tells what it does (8:11).

decisions.choice: blew his trumpet
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to blow a trumpet. Every level says so plainly; "his trumpet" is supplied.

source.text: καὶ τὸ ὄνομα τοῦ ἀστέρος λέγεται· ὁ Ἄψινθος.

records.literal_gloss: And the name of the star is called the Wormwood.

en.L: And the name of the star is called Wormwood.
en.R: The name of the star is Wormwood. Wormwood is a very bitter plant.

fr.L: Et le nom de l’étoile se dit Absinthe.
fr.R: Le nom de l’étoile est Absinthe. L’absinthe est une plante très amère.

es.L: Y el nombre de la estrella se dice Ajenjo.
es.R: El nombre de la estrella es Ajenjo. El ajenjo es una planta muy amarga.

decisions.choice: Wormwood: a bitter plant, a picture of judgment
decisions.reason: Wormwood is a plant with a very bitter taste. In the prophets it stands for the bitterness of God's judgment: "I will feed this people with wormwood and give them poisonous water to drink" (Jeremiah 9:15; 23:15).

decisions.choice: Wormwood is a very bitter plant (R)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name (m1).

decisions.choice: Absinthe
decisions.reason: "Absinthe" is the French name of the bitter plant the English calls wormwood (m1), and the traditional name of the star. Readers may know the word as a liqueur, so Readable says it is a plant, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: Ajenjo
decisions.reason: "Ajenjo" is the Spanish name of the bitter plant, so the star keeps the plant's name as in the Greek; Readable explains the plant, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ τρίτον τῶν ὑδάτων εἰς ἄψινθον, καὶ πολλοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀπέθανον ἐκ τῶν ὑδάτων, ὅτι ἐπικράνθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And became the third of the waters into wormwood, and many of the people died from the waters because they were made bitter.

en.L: And a third of the waters became wormwood, and many of the {{gender:people|men}} died from the waters, because they had been made bitter.
en.B: A third of the waters turned to wormwood, and many {{gender:people|men}} died from the water, because it had been made bitter.
en.R: A third of the water became bitter like wormwood. Many {{gender:people|men}} died from drinking the water, because it was bitter.

fr.L: Et le tiers des eaux devint de l’absinthe, et beaucoup {{gender:de gens|d’hommes}} moururent à cause des eaux, parce qu’elles avaient été rendues amères.
fr.B: Le tiers des eaux se changea en absinthe, et beaucoup {{gender:de gens|d’hommes}} moururent à cause de l’eau, parce qu’elle était devenue amère.
fr.R: Un tiers de l’eau est devenu amer comme l’absinthe. Beaucoup {{gender:de gens|d’hommes}} sont morts parce qu’ils avaient bu cette eau amère.

es.L: Y la tercera parte de las aguas se convirtió en ajenjo, y {{gender:muchas de las personas|muchos de los hombres}} murieron a causa de las aguas, porque habían sido hechas amargas.
es.B: La tercera parte de las aguas se convirtió en ajenjo, y {{gender:muchas personas|muchos hombres}} murieron por causa del agua, porque se había vuelto amarga.
es.R: La tercera parte del agua se volvió amarga como el ajenjo. {{gender:Muchas personas|Muchos hombres}} murieron por beber esa agua, porque estaba amarga.

decisions.choice: bitter water: Marah reversed
decisions.reason: At Marah God made bitter water sweet for Israel (Exodus 15:23-25). Here sweet water is made bitter and deadly. Wormwood itself is not a deadly poison; the picture is of water turned so bitter that it brings death (compare Jeremiah 9:15).

decisions.choice: people: men and women
decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων means human beings in general.

decisions.choice: people | men
decisions.reason: The gender setting, since the word includes everyone (m2).

decisions.choice: {{gender:muchas personas|muchos hombres}}
decisions.reason: The Greek word means human beings, men and women, as the meaning decision says. Spanish follows the English gender setting, with "personas" by default and the older "hombres" as the alternative; the span takes in the words that agree with the noun.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ τέταρτος ἄγγελος ἐσάλπισεν· καὶ ἐπλήγη τὸ τρίτον τοῦ ἡλίου καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῆς σελήνης καὶ τὸ τρίτον τῶν ἀστέρων, ἵνα σκοτισθῇ τὸ τρίτον αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ ἡμέρα μὴ φάνῃ τὸ τρίτον αὐτῆς, καὶ ἡ νὺξ ὁμοίως.

records.literal_gloss: And the fourth angel blew trumpet, and was struck the third of the sun and the third of the moon and the third of the stars, so that would be darkened the third of them and the day not would shine the third of it, and the night likewise.

en.L: And the fourth angel blew his trumpet, and a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them would be darkened, and the day would not shine for a third of it, and the night likewise.
en.B: Then the fourth angel blew his trumpet. A blow fell on a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, and a third of their light was darkened: for a third of the day nothing shone, and so too for the night.
en.R: The fourth angel blew his trumpet. Then a third of the sun, a third of the moon, and a third of the stars were struck. They became dark. So there was no light for a third of the day and for a third of the night.

fr.L: Et le quatrième ange sonna de la trompette ; et le tiers du soleil fut frappé, et le tiers de la lune, et le tiers des étoiles, afin que le tiers d’entre eux soit obscurci, et que le jour ne brille pas pendant le tiers [de sa durée], et la nuit de même.
fr.B: Puis le quatrième ange sonna de la trompette. Un coup frappa le tiers du soleil, le tiers de la lune et le tiers des étoiles, et le tiers de leur lumière s’obscurcit : pendant un tiers du jour, rien ne brilla, et de même pendant la nuit.
fr.R: Le quatrième ange a sonné de la trompette. Alors un tiers du soleil, un tiers de la lune et un tiers des étoiles ont été frappés. Ils sont devenus sombres. Il n’y a donc plus eu de lumière pendant un tiers du jour et pendant un tiers de la nuit.

es.L: Y el cuarto ángel tocó la trompeta, y fue herida la tercera parte del sol, y la tercera parte de la luna, y la tercera parte de las estrellas, para que se oscureciera la tercera parte de ellos, y el día no brillara en su tercera parte, y la noche de la misma manera.
es.B: Entonces el cuarto ángel tocó su trompeta. Fueron heridos la tercera parte del sol, la tercera parte de la luna y la tercera parte de las estrellas, de modo que se oscureció la tercera parte de su luz: durante la tercera parte del día no hubo luz, y lo mismo sucedió con la noche.
es.R: El cuarto ángel tocó su trompeta. Entonces fueron heridos la tercera parte del sol, la tercera parte de la luna y la tercera parte de las estrellas. Se oscurecieron. Así no hubo luz durante la tercera parte del día ni durante la tercera parte de la noche.

decisions.choice: an echo of the plagues of Egypt: darkness
decisions.reason: The trumpets recall the plagues God sent on Egypt before the exodus (Exodus 10:21-23). As then, God judges a power that oppresses his people, and those he has sealed are spared (7:3; 9:4).

decisions.choice: a third darkened: dimmer, or dark for a third of the time
decisions.reason: The sentence says both that a third of the lights are darkened and that the day does not shine for a third of its length. The picture is not meant to be worked out like an eclipse; it is a partial darkness, as in Amos 8:9, where God makes the sun go down at noon.

decisions.choice: blew his trumpet
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to blow a trumpet. Every level says so plainly; "his trumpet" is supplied.

decisions.choice: fue herida (L); fueron heridos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek verb is the word for striking with a blow, the plague word. Spanish "herir" keeps that picture of being struck without saying how; the meaning decision leaves open whether the light was dimmed or failed for part of the time.

source.text: Καὶ εἶδον, καὶ ἤκουσα ἑνὸς ἀετοῦ πετομένου ἐν μεσουρανήματι λέγοντος φωνῇ μεγάλῃ· Οὐαὶ οὐαὶ οὐαὶ τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἐκ τῶν λοιπῶν φωνῶν τῆς σάλπιγγος τῶν τριῶν ἀγγέλων τῶν μελλόντων σαλπίζειν.

records.literal_gloss: And I saw, and I heard one eagle flying in mid-heaven saying with a voice loud: Woe woe woe to those dwelling on the earth from the remaining voices of the trumpet of the three angels the [ones] being about to blow trumpet.

en.L: And I looked, and I heard an eagle flying in mid-heaven, saying with a loud voice, "Woe, woe, woe to those who live on the earth, because of the remaining blasts of the trumpet of the three angels who are about to blow!"
en.B: Then I looked, and I heard an eagle flying high overhead call out in a loud voice: "Woe, woe, woe to those who live on the earth, at the blasts of the trumpets that the three remaining angels are about to blow!"
en.R: As I watched, I heard an eagle flying high in the sky. It called out in a loud voice, "How terrible! How terrible! How terrible it will be for the people who live on the earth! Three more angels are about to blow their trumpets, and terrible things will happen!"

fr.L: Et je vis, et j’entendis un aigle qui volait au milieu du ciel, disant d’une voix forte : « Malheur, malheur, malheur à ceux qui habitent sur la terre, à cause des autres sonneries de la trompette des trois anges qui vont sonner ! »
fr.B: Puis je regardai, et j’entendis un aigle qui volait très haut dans le ciel crier d’une voix forte : « Malheur, malheur, malheur aux habitants de la terre, à cause des sonneries de trompette que les trois derniers anges vont faire entendre ! »
fr.R: Pendant que je regardais, j’ai entendu un aigle qui volait très haut dans le ciel. Il a crié d’une voix forte : « Quel malheur ! Quel malheur ! Quel malheur pour les gens qui habitent sur la terre ! Trois autres anges vont sonner de la trompette, et des choses terribles vont arriver ! »

es.L: Y miré, y oí un águila que volaba en medio del cielo, diciendo a gran voz: «¡Ay, ay, ay de los que habitan sobre la tierra, a causa de los toques restantes de la trompeta de los tres ángeles que están a punto de tocar!».
es.B: Entonces miré, y oí a un águila que volaba en lo alto del cielo y gritaba con voz fuerte: «¡Ay, ay, ay de los que habitan en la tierra, por los toques de trompeta que están a punto de dar los tres ángeles que quedan!».
es.R: Mientras miraba, oí un águila que volaba en lo alto del cielo. Gritaba con voz fuerte: «¡Qué terrible! ¡Qué terrible! ¡Qué terrible será para la gente que vive en la tierra! Otros tres ángeles están a punto de tocar sus trompetas, y van a suceder cosas terribles».

decisions.choice: an eagle
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads "eagle". Some later manuscripts read "angel". The translation follows the SBLGNT. Reviewers should check this against the SBLGNT apparatus.

decisions.choice: an eagle in mid-heaven: a messenger seen and heard by all
decisions.reason: μεσουρανήματι is the highest point of the sky, where the sun stands at noon, so that everyone can see and hear. Hosea 8:1 pictures an eagle over the house of the LORD as a sign of coming judgment. ἑνὸς "one" here means "an".

decisions.choice: three woes for the three trumpets still to come
decisions.reason: "Woe" is a cry of grief and warning. The three woes belong to the fifth, sixth and seventh trumpets (9:12; 11:14). They fall on "those who live on the earth", the world that opposes God (3:10; 6:10).

decisions.choice: Woe (L, B); How terrible (R)
decisions.reason: "Woe" is the familiar word in English Bibles for this cry. Readable says what it means.

decisions.choice: Malheur (L, B); Quel malheur ! (R) (for the whole chapter and the woes that follow)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term: "Malheur à" is the French cry of woe. Readable makes it an exclamation that young readers know, "Quel malheur !", which says what the English "How terrible" says.

decisions.choice: ¡Ay, ay, ay de ...! (L, B); ¡Qué terrible! (R)
decisions.reason: "¡Ay de ...!" is the settled Spanish for this cry of grief and warning in the Gospels, and it is kept for the three woes through the book; Readable says "¡Qué terrible será para ...!", as the Spanish Gospels do and as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: en medio del cielo (L); en lo alto del cielo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Greek word names the highest point of the sky, where the sun stands at noon, so the eagle is seen and heard by everyone, as the meaning decision says. Literal keeps "en medio del cielo", and Balanced and Readable say "en lo alto del cielo".
